memory_update.text: ANET is a core direct candidate for the AI Ethernet switching systems layer; prioritize verification of AI-specific networking revenue, 800G/1.6T mix, and cloud concentration.
AVGO is a core direct candidate across custom AI ASICs, Ethernet switching/routing, NICs, PCIe, and optical interconnect; its node exposure is broad but needs revenue disaggregation.
MRVL is a core direct candidate for AI optical DSPs, DCI modules, SerDes, PCIe/CXL connectivity, Ethernet switching silicon, and custom AI silicon.
COHR is a core optical candidate for AI data-center photonics, transceivers, lasers, CPO/pluggable roadmap, and optical circuit switching.

ALAB is a direct high-growth connectivity candidate for rack-scale AI systems, especially PCIe, CXL, Ethernet, UALink, NVLink Fusion-related connectivity, active cable modules, and connectivity software.

CSCO was not included due to the five-candidate limit but remains an obvious leader to test in a broader networking systems pass, especially Silicon One, Nexus, AI PODs, optics, and hyperscaler AI infrastructure orders.

LITE and FN were not included due to the five-candidate limit but remain important optical supply-chain candidates: Lumentum for lasers/transceivers and Fabrinet for optical module manufacturing/advanced packaging.

The AI networking chokepoint should be split into at least four subnodes for later scoring: Ethernet switching systems, merchant/custom networking silicon, optical DSPs/interconnect silicon, and optical modules/components/manufacturing.

Primary US-listed AI networking candidates for this node: AVGO for merchant Ethernet switching silicon and connectivity chips; ANET for AI Ethernet switching systems; MRVL for optical DSP/coherent interconnect; LITE for lasers/OCS/optical components; CRDO for AEC/optical DSP/SerDes connectivity.

The chokepoint logic is strongest where bandwidth transitions require new silicon or scarce optical components: 800G to 1.6T Ethernet switching, 400G/lane optical DSPs, EML/laser supply, active electrical cables, and OCS for scale-up/scale-across networks.

Next pass should test additional US-listed second-order names not included due to the 5-candidate cap: COHR for transceivers/VCSELs/EMLs/CPO/OCS, FN for optical manufacturing, CLS for AI-scale 1.6TbE switch platforms and supply-chain execution, ALAB for PCIe/CXL/Ethernet rack-scale connectivity, CIEN for DCI/coherent optical systems, GLW/APH for fiber/connectors, CSCO/JNPR for competing Ethernet systems, and KEYS for test equipment.

Need a separate falsification pass on whether Ethernet share gains are actually occurring in back-end AI networks versus Nvidia InfiniBand/Spectrum-X, and whether hyperscalers are internalizing more networking silicon or optics.
CRDO should be tracked as a direct AI networking interconnect candidate because its optical DSPs, AECs, and Microsoft HiWire Switch AEC relationship map to rack/ToR and transceiver connectivity.

COHR and LITE are direct optical-component candidates for 800G/1.6T AI networking; key differentiators to verify are InP/EML capacity, silicon photonics transition risk, and customer qualification depth.
FN is a second-order optical manufacturing capacity candidate; AI linkage is less direct and requires customer and product mix verification.
KEYS maps to the validation chokepoint: 1.6T Ethernet, optical/copper interconnects, 224G lanes, and AI data-center network emulation may become gating items before mass deployment.
SMTC was not included in the 5-candidate limit but remains a follow-up candidate for LPO, PMD/TIA/laser-driver, and low-power optical analog exposure to AI data-center networking.

summary: Combined focused Layer 1B searches: Expanded the US-listed universe for the AI data-center networking node to five high-directness candidates across Ethernet switching systems, custom/networking silicon, optical DSP/interconnect silicon, optical modules/components, and rack-scale connectivity. This is a research universe only, not a ranking or trading recommendation. The strongest direct exposure candidates are Arista Networks, Broadcom, Marvell Technology, Coherent, and Astera Labs. Cisco, Lumentum, Fabrinet, and other optical/component names remain coverage gaps for a later wider pass because the candidate limit is five. Expanded the US-listed universe around AI data-center networking bottlenecks. The highest-priority direct exposures in this pass are merchant Ethernet switching silicon, AI Ethernet switch systems, optical DSPs, lasers/OCS, and active electrical/optical interconnect components. This is research support only, not a trading recommendation. Expanded the US-listed universe around AI data-center networking beyond the obvious Ethernet switch and ASIC leaders. The strongest second-order mappings found in this pass are optical/component suppliers, active electrical cable and DSP silicon, optical manufacturing services, and validation/test infrastructure for 800G/1.6T Ethernet and optical interconnect. These are research candidates only, not recommendations.
